newsitem.title: UK: Czech Export Bank aims to lengthen bond maturities.
newsitem.headline: Czech Export Bank aims to lengthen bond maturities.

text.p: The Czech government's export credit agency, Czech Export Bank, aims to extend the maturity of its bonds in order to match exporters' funding needs, chief executive Miroslava Hrncirova said at a presentation on Wednesday.
"Five years is not the only maturity we will be looking at...we need longer-dated bonds as well," she said, speaking ahead of the launch of Czech Export Bank's (CEB) debut Eurobond.
CEB will launch a $150 million five-year bond on Thursday. JP Morgan will lead manage the transaction expected to be priced to yield in the low 50 basis point area over U.S. Treasury notes.
Hrncirova said while exporters needed dollars the most, CEB might also consider tapping the mark sector, but that exporters had no need for Czech crown bonds.
CEB -- which enjoys full government guarantee -- was established in March 1995 to increase Czech exports by providing exporters with competitive financing.
Hrncirova said CEB provided long-term financing from the outset.

"This is where the market needs us, because commercial banks can easily provide financing for three or four years, but its more difficult for exporters to go on their own for seven years or more," she said.

CEB has thus far concluded five loan transactions totalling $320 -- half with a maturity greater than five years and the other half with a maturity less than five years -- and there are six loan transactions close to completion totalling $540 million, Hrncirova said.
In the next two to three years CEB aims to conclude around 61 loan transactions totalling $3.3 billion.
The average size of each transaction is around $60 to $100 million.
Hrncirova said the CEB did not want to assume the role of the private banking system, but to assist it.

CEB has a share capital of 1.5 billion Czech crowns ($48.5 million) and employs around 90 people with headquarters in Prague. It also has insurance from the Export Guarantee and Insurance Corporation (EGAP).
Hrncirova said CEB was "very glad" with the recently awarded credit ratings. "Its what we expected," she said.
Moody's Investors Service rated CEB's upcoming five-year dollar deal Baa1 while Standard & Poor's rated a long-term rating of A to the bond.
